errors.text_span: The horizontal axis lists the model names – including “gpt-4o-2024-11-20”, “Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M”, and “Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407”, among others – and is labeled accordingly. The vertical axis represents percentage values, with a linear scale ranging from 0% to 100%, with tick marks every 20%.
errors.evidence: In the figure, the model names are on the vertical axis (y-axis), while the percentages are on the horizontal axis (x-axis). The x-axis shows percent values and the y-axis lists model categories.

errors.text_span: Each model’s performance is represented by a set of three horizontally stacked bars, one for each category.
errors.evidence: The bars are grouped horizontally for each model, not stacked. Each model has three separate bars corresponding to Understanding, Reasoning, and Trustworthiness placed side by side in separate panels.

errors.text_span: The “Understanding” bars are light blue, “Reasoning” bars are medium blue, and “Trustworthiness” bars are dark blue.
errors.evidence: The color mapping is incorrect. In the figure, the Understanding bars are dark blue, Reasoning bars are medium blue, and Trustworthiness bars are light blue.

errors.text_span: For instance, “gpt-4o-2024-11-20” has a light blue “Understanding” bar extending to 98.0%, a medium blue “Reasoning” bar extending to 34.9%, and a dark blue “Trustworthiness” bar extending to 66.5%.
errors.evidence: The values are assigned to the wrong categories for Trustworthiness and Understanding. For gpt-4o-2024-11-20, Understanding is 98.0, Reasoning is 66.5, and Trustworthiness is 54.6.

errors.text_span: a dark blue “Trustworthiness” bar extending to 66.5%.
errors.evidence: 66.5% is the Reasoning value for gpt-4o-2024-11-20, not Trustworthiness; the Trustworthiness value is 54.6%.

errors.text_span: Representative values for the shortest bar set are 2.4% for Understanding, 7.2% for Reasoning, and 0.0% for Trustworthiness, while the tallest bar set has 98.0% for Understanding, 34.9% for Reasoning, and 66.5% for Trustworthiness.
errors.evidence: The shortest model set does have 2.4% Understanding and 7.2% Reasoning, but its Trustworthiness is 0.0%, while the tallest set's Reasoning and Trustworthiness values are not 34.9% and 66.5% together. The tallest Understanding value is 98.0%, but the corresponding Reasoning and Trustworthiness values for that model are 66.5% and 54.6%.

errors.text_span: Bars are sorted vertically in descending order based on the height of the “Understanding” portion; the tallest bar set is at the top and the shortest is at the bottom.
errors.evidence: The models are indeed ordered roughly by Understanding descending, but there is no 'stacked' bar set or 'height of the Understanding portion' because the figure uses separate horizontal bars in three panels. The description mischaracterizes the structure while describing the ordering.
